title: Perfect direct image over a Noetherian base
statement: Let S be Noetherian, let f:X\to S be of finite presentation [def-pc-morphism-conventions], let E_i be perfect on X [def-pc-perfect-complex], and let G^\bullet be bounded, finitely presented, flat over S, with proper support [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Then Rf_*(E_i\otimes^L G^\bullet) [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is perfect on S [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Since S is Noetherian and f is of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type [def-pc-morphism-conventions] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], X is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] (Stacks, Morphisms, Lemma 29.15.6, Tag 01T6). So each finitely presented term G^i is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], and coherent modules on a locally Noetherian scheme form an abelian subcategory closed under kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums (Stacks, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.9.2, Tag 01Y0). Let Z=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Supp}(G^i), a closed subset proper over S by the proper-support hypothesis on G^\bullet [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; as S is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, Z is quasi-compact. Because E is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], finitely many opens U_1,\dots,U_n cover Z with E|_{U_j} isomorphic to a strictly perfect complex P_j^\bullet, whose terms are direct summands of finite free modules, hence flat; so on U_j the object E\otimes^L G^\bullet is the bounded total complex of P_j^\bullet\otimes G^\bullet, whose terms are direct summands of finite direct sums of the G^i, and on X\setminus Z it is zero. Hence E\otimes^L G^\bullet has coherent cohomology sheaves (coherence is local), nonzero only in the finite range of degrees given by the n complexes P_j^\bullet\otimes G^\bullet.

source.place: Lemma 36.27.2, Tag 0DJQ, proof: coherence of the cohomology of E tensor^L G

proof.text: Every cohomology sheaf of E\otimes^L G^\bullet is zero on X\setminus Z (step 1), so its support, closed because the sheaf is coherent, lies in Z. A closed subset of Z is proper over S, since a closed immersion is proper and properness is stable under composition; so each cohomology sheaf has support proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base].

source.place: Lemma 36.27.2, Tag 0DJQ, proof: support of E tensor^L G

proof.text: Each G^i is flat over S, i.e. flat as an f^{-1}\mathcal O_S-module, and so are direct summands of finite direct sums of them. So, viewed in D(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S), the object E\otimes^L G^\bullet is zero on X\setminus Z and on each U_j of step 1 is represented by a complex of flat modules in the fixed finite range [a,b] of degrees containing those of all P_j^\bullet\otimes G^\bullet. By Stacks, Cohomology, Lemma 20.48.3 (Tag 08CI) its restriction to each of these opens has tor-amplitude in [a,b]; as tor-amplitude is the vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of E\otimes^L_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_S}\mathcal F outside [a,b] (Definition 20.48.1, Tag 08CG), a local condition, E\otimes^L G^\bullet has finite Tor dimension as an object of D(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S).

source.place: Lemma 36.27.2, Tag 0DJQ, proof: 'The hypothesis on the tor dimension also follows as G^i is flat over f^{-1}O_S'

proof.text: Since f is locally of finite type (step 1) and S is Noetherian, steps 1 to 3 give the hypotheses of the Noetherian direct-image criterion [lem-pc-bounded-coherent-finite-tor-proper-pushforward-perfect] (Stacks Tag 08EV) for E\otimes^L G^\bullet. Its conclusion is exactly that Rf_*(E\otimes^L G^\bullet) is perfect on S [def-pc-perfect-complex].
